## Claims
- [source-backed] For \(v_{r,s,t,n}\), \(i=s-t+1\), \(j=r-t+1\), and Theorem 4.8 gives the lower-adjoined generating family \(\{s_\mu:i^j\subseteq\mu\subseteq(i^j,b^a)\}\), of cardinality \(\binom{a+b}{a}\). [doi:10.1090/s0002-9947-2010-05163-3, lines 847-891]
- [source-backed] For \(n=4m\), \(r=n-r=2m\), and \(i=j=m\), one has \(a=b=m\) and \(J_{v_{r,s,t,n}}=I_{w_{r,s,t,n}}\). [doi:10.1090/s0002-9947-2010-05163-3, lines 938-955]
- [proved] Assuming the accepted internal minimality theorem in its numerical form, the ideal
  \[
  I_{w_{2m,2m,m+1,4m}}
  \]
  requires at least \(\binom{2m}{m}\) homogeneous generators; hence it has an exponential generator lower bound.

## Strategy
Let
\[
v_m=v_{2m,2m,m+1,4m}.
\]
It is admissible, and
\[
i=s-t+1=m,\qquad j=r-t+1=m,\qquad
a=\min(2m-m,2m-m)=m,\quad b=m.
\]
The lower-adjoined family is therefore
\[
\mathcal F_m=\{\bar s_\mu:m^m\subseteq\mu\subseteq m^{2m}\}.
\]
Its members correspond to partitions inside an \(m\times m\) rectangle, hence
\[
|\mathcal F_m|=\binom{2m}{m}.
\]
The accepted internal minimality theorem gives
\[
\mu(J_{v_m})=|\mathcal F_m|=\binom{2m}{m}.
\]
The cited reduction gives \(J_{v_m}=I_{w_{2m,2m,m+1,4m}}\), so
\[
\mu(I_{w_{2m,2m,m+1,4m}})=\binom{2m}{m}.
\]
Finally,
\[
\binom{2m}{m}\ge \frac{4^m}{2m+1}
=\frac{2^{n/2}}{n/2+1}\qquad(n=4m),
\]
which is exponential in \(n\). The sharper asymptotic is
\[
\binom{2m}{m}\sim\frac{4^m}{\sqrt{\pi m}}
=\frac{\sqrt2^{\,n+2}}{\sqrt{\pi n}}.
\]

## Gaps
The deduction requires the internal minimality theorem to assert a numerical lower bound (or equivalent indecomposable-rank statement), not merely inclusion-irredundancy of \(\mathcal F_m\).

## Next
The requested exponential lower-bound corollary is established relative to that accepted internal theorem.
